sources.title: New gigabit address checker launches
facts: The address checker launched on 13 March 2026 for England and Wales.
It reports whether an address is within government-backed or commercial rollout plans.
The release cites more than 750 premises per day using assured December 2025 delivery data.
Premises outside current plans are redirected to Ofcom supplier information.
Checker and press-release outputs must preserve plan status and publication vintage rather than being treated as live service guarantees.

sources.title: 50th UK Government-funded 4G mast goes live in rural Scotland
facts: Fifty UK Government-funded 4G masts had been activated in Scotland by 9 July 2026.
The Scottish upgrades provide all-operator 4G coverage across more than 1,900 square kilometres.
Across Great Britain, more than 140 government-funded SRN masts had been activated.
The SRN reached 95% UK landmass coverage from at least one operator ahead of schedule.
Scotland's all-operator coverage rose from 41% to 71%, but these are national-area aggregates rather than address guarantees.

sources.title: DSIT Main Estimate memorandum 2026 to 2027
facts: DSIT states continued funding for Project Gigabit and the Shared Rural Network.
The 2026-27 capital budget includes a £114 million increase for Project Gigabit.
It includes a £47 million increase for SRN delivery slippage, including £34.3 million budget exchange.
Project Gigabit has a 99% premises-by-2032 objective and an AMBER delivery confidence assessment.
Outstanding legally binding SRN spectrum obligations remain due by January 2027.

sources.title: Mobile Market Review: call for evidence
facts: The call for evidence was updated on 27 March 2026.
Government retains an ambition for all populated areas to have standalone 5G by 2030.
The document reports standalone 5G extending to 83% of UK premises at its stated reference point.
Mobile data consumption increased 495% between 2018 and 2025.
Non-terrestrial networks and satellite services are included within advanced connectivity technologies, but policy evidence is not current parcel coverage.

sources.title: Revocation of the 2 GHz Mobile Satellite Services Regulations
facts: The government response was published on 12 January 2026.
Eight responses were received from interested parties.
The existing two mobile satellite service licences expire on 13 May 2027.
Revocation is intended to avoid restrictions on future use of the 2 GHz band.
Future Ofcom authorisation under domestic law is a regulatory pathway, not proof of deployed connectivity.

sources.title: £30 million C-LEO satellite communications investment
facts: A second C-LEO funding round provides £30 million for UK satellite communications technologies.
The announcement was published on 4 March 2026.
The programme targets components and technologies for low-Earth-orbit satellite constellations.
The first C-LEO call supported three projects with £18 million and eight UK companies.
Technology funding and market-readiness claims do not establish service availability at a property.

sources.title: Rural Connectivity Accelerator programme: projects
facts: The programme studies business connectivity needs in rural and very hard to reach areas.
Pilots examine hybrid combinations of broadband, satellite and wireless networks.
Objectives include viability testing, business connectivity and stackable use cases.
Hybrid satellite-terrestrial technologies remain at an early trial stage.
Proof-of-concept outcomes require scalability, replicability and sustainability evidence before operational promotion.
